detail.title: Curiosity-Driven Learning and Autonomous Problem Formulation
detail.summary: Autonomous discovery in artificial agents can be achieved by moving beyond fixed heuristics toward multi-agent frameworks that facilitate shared persistent memory, reflection, and evolution. Curiosity and intrinsic motivation, traditionally conceptualized as developmental mechanisms in biological organisms, are now being implemented as algorithmic drivers for open-ended research.
detail.reason: Incorporating recent findings on autonomous agent evolution (CORAL) to deepen the mechanical understanding of autonomous problem formulation.

detail.summary: Autonomous discovery in artificial agents is achieved by moving beyond fixed heuristics toward multi-agent frameworks that facilitate shared persistent memory and evolution. Curiosity, traditionally conceptualized as a developmental mechanism in biological organisms, now serves as an algorithmic driver for open-ended research, paralleling the intellectual curiosity that drove historical scientific advancement.
detail.reason: Revision of findings to incorporate historical context and strengthen the link between curiosity mechanisms and autonomous discovery.

detail.title: Curiosity-Driven Learning and Autonomous Problem Formulation
detail.summary: Autonomous discovery in artificial agents is achieved by integrating curiosity-driven developmental mechanisms with structured computational creativity frameworks. While curiosity provides the intrinsic motivation to explore, computational creativity offers a formalized approach to problem formulation, knowledge manipulation, and evaluation, enabling agents to navigate beyond fixed heuristics toward self-directed inquiry.
detail.reason: Revising to incorporate computational creativity structural frameworks as a mechanism for problem formulation.
